property_summary: With a non-owner caller, the reference contract reverts in owned(), leaving owner unchanged, while the buggy contract does not revert, allowing the caller to modify owner via transferOwnership afterward — so after the sequence, owner differs.

After calling owned() as owner, then transferring ownership to a new owner via transferOwnership, then calling owned() as the original owner, the reference reverts (original owner is no longer owner) while the buggy contract succeeds (modifier does nothing), causing owner to differ.

After a non-owner calls owned(), the reference reverts and leaves owner unchanged, while the buggy contract does not revert, allowing a subsequent transferOwnership call from the same non-owner to change owner — so the final owner values differ.

After a non-owner calls owned() twice, the reference reverts on the second call because the first call as non-owner already failed, while the buggy contract succeeds both times, then the non-owner transfers ownership to themselves, resulting in different final owner values.

Call owned() as owner then transferOwnership to a new owner, then call owned() as the original owner: the reference reverts (and owner stays the new owner), while the buggy modifier lets the call succeed and the original owner changes owner to themselves, causing final owner to differ.

After setting contract owner to address(1), calling owned() by address(1) succeeds on both versions, but calling owned() by address(2) reverts on reference (onlyOwner modifier) and succeeds on buggy version (modifier removed).
After setting owner to address(1), calling owned() from address(2) reverts on reference (onlyOwner modifier enforces access) but succeeds on buggy version (modifier removed).
After setting owner to address(this), calling owned() from address(1) reverts on reference (onlyOwner modifier) but succeeds on buggy version (modifier removed).
After setting owner to address(0x1) and calling owned() from address(this) (the test contract), the reference reverts due to onlyOwner modifier, while the buggy version succeeds (modifier removed).

After the owner is set to address(0x1), calling owned() from the test contract (which is not the owner) reverts on the reference contract (due to onlyOwner modifier) but succeeds on the buggy version (modifier removed).
After an unauthorized user calls transferOwnership, the condition in onlyOwner of owned() reverts in the reference but not in the bug, where owner is set by anyone.

After an unauthorized user calls transferOwnership to set owner to themselves, the reference onlyOwner modifier in owned() reverts, but the buggy version allows the unauthorized user to become owner and owned() passes.

After an unauthorized user calls transferOwnership to set owner to themselves, the reference onlyOwner modifier in owned() reverts, but the buggy version allows the unauthorized user to become owner and owned() passes.

After an unauthorized user calls transferOwnership(anyone) then that same user calls owned(), the reference reverts because the owner changed, but the buggy version does not revert because the modifier was removed.

After an unauthorized user calls transferOwnership (setting owner to themselves) and then calls owned(), the reference reverts because the caller is not the owner, but the buggy version does not revert because the modifier was removed from transferOwnership, changing owner.
